Repo: ai-product-copy (APC Shopify app; Firebase Functions packages/functions/src, Koa; jest from repo root). Brief: second-brain jobs/2026-10-06-security-backlog.md.

Move cross-app store-data routes off integration keys before BFCM (brief A1).
- routes/proxy.js: GET /proxy/shop/apc, POST /proxy/apc/bfcm-sale and /proxy/apc/bfcm-sale/deactivate use validateAccessToken, which (since FAL-720) requires integration.shopId — but all 4 prod integrationKeys have no shopId, so these return 403 for the SEO/Blog backends (1x403 already on /shop/apc) and BFCM in November will fail. Move them to the existing middleware/requireSiblingApp.js (BUNDLE_SIBLING_KEY_SEO / BUNDLE_SIBLING_KEY_BLOG). Verified by hash on prod CI vars: SEO sends AVADA_SEO_ON_APC_PRO_ACCESS_TOKEN == APC BUNDLE_SIBLING_KEY_SEO, Blog sends AVADA_AI_PRODUCT_COPY_PRO_ACCESS_TOKEN == APC BUNDLE_SIBLING_KEY_BLOG — and both env vars hold the SAME value on prod, so ctx.state.siblingApp cannot distinguish SEO from Blog: do NOT restrict BFCM to one sibling (comment why in one line).
- Handlers that take shop from the X-SEO-Shop-Domain header keep doing so (sibling keys are app-level by design); whitelist any body fields spread into shop data if a handler spreads ctx.req.body.
- Test: packages/functions/src/__tests__/proxyRoutes.sibling.test.js pinning wiring on routes source + middleware behaviour (merchant key 401, sibling key passes).

Rules: touch only the files in the contract allow list. Comments say WHY only (a constraint, a Shopify limit, an ordering), never narrate WHAT; no step numbering, no banners. Never write a secret/token literal anywhere (code, tests, comments, logs) — tests use obviously fake values. Do not modify .env*, lockfiles, .gitlab-ci.yml, firebase.json unless listed. Do not add dependencies. Run the verify commands yourself before saying done. Write the exploit-before-fix scenario and file:line of each change in your final message (it goes into the MR).
